title: Agentforce Specialist Certification - Practice Exam
description: 60-question timed practice exam mirroring the official Spring '26 Agentforce Specialist blueprint domain weights. 105 minutes, pass with 72% or higher.

questions.question: Zero data retention is best described as which of the following?
options: A per-agent setting an admin toggles on the agent record
A feature that stops Salesforce from logging anything
A guarantee that grounded data never leaves the org
The platform's standing agreement with external partner providers, so the provider retains nothing and trains on nothing
questions.explanation: Zero data retention is an agreement between Salesforce and external partner providers such as OpenAI and Azure OpenAI that they retain no data and train on none, while Salesforce still stores prompts and responses in Data 360 for the audit trail.

questions.question: A requirement is to fill a Next Step text field on an Opportunity record page with a generated suggestion when a user clicks a button. Which template type fits?
options: Field Generation, which binds one object and writes generated text into a record field
Sales Email, which drafts an email
Record Summary, which summarizes a record
Flex, which defines its own multi-object resources
questions.explanation: The output lands in a field on a single record and is triggered from the record page, which is exactly what Field Generation is built for.

questions.question: Which Trust Layer feature keeps prompts and responses from being retained by third-party model providers and from being used to train their models?
options: Data masking
Zero data retention
Toxicity scoring
Secure data retrieval
questions.explanation: Zero data retention is the agreement with the external partner providers that says they retain no data and train on none, while data masking hides sensitive values, toxicity scoring rates content, and secure data retrieval governs grounding.

questions.question: An admin needs to let a group of service reps run an already-built prompt template without letting them edit it. Which permission set fits?
options: Prompt Template Manager
Prompt Template User
Customize Application
Modify All Data
questions.explanation: The Prompt Template User permission set grants only Execute Prompt Templates, which is run-without-author, while Prompt Template Manager adds authoring and Customize Application is unnecessarily broad.

questions.question: A requirement asks for a personalized welcome email drafted from each Contact record, tailored in tone and reused across the sales team. Which tool fits?
options: A formula field on Contact
A validation rule
A scheduled Flow that updates a field
A prompt template in Prompt Builder, grounded in the Contact record
questions.explanation: The requirement is generated language grounded in record data, which is exactly the shape Prompt Builder serves, while a formula, a validation rule, and a Flow compute or enforce values rather than generate prose.

questions.question: What does the Trust Layer do with the placeholder-to-value mapping it creates during masking?
options: It sends the mapping to the model as context
It stores the mapping permanently in the audit trail
It keeps the mapping only temporarily and uses it to demask the response
It discards the mapping immediately with no demasking
questions.explanation: The Trust Layer temporarily stores the relationship between the original entity and its placeholder and uses that stored mapping to put the real value back into the response, which is why the user still sees their own data.

questions.question: A policy page changes daily and an agent must always state the current version. Which grounding approach fits?
options: A vector retriever over the policy documents
An action that reads the current record at run time rather than a retriever over an index
An ensemble retriever across all sources
A merge field on the case that stores a copy of the policy
questions.explanation: A retriever reads an index that refreshes on a schedule, so a fact that changes daily can be served stale, while an action that reads the record at run time always returns the current value.

questions.question: A requirement must combine an Account, its Opportunities, and a custom Product object into one generated recommendation, and the output is used outside a record field. Which type fits?
options: Field Generation
Record Summary
Flex, which can define multiple objects as resources and is invoked from Flow, Apex, or a prompt action
Sales Email
questions.explanation: Flex is the type that defines its own resources and can ground with more than one object, while Field Generation and Record Summary bind a single object and Sales Email binds a Contact or Lead.

questions.question: Which two methods does the Trust Layer use to identify sensitive data for masking?
options: Pattern-based and field-based detection
Manual tagging and user flags
Encryption and hashing
Apex triggers and validation rules
questions.explanation: Detection is pattern-based, using regex and context with machine learning for values such as names, and field-based, using the metadata on fields classified with Shield Platform Encryption or Data Classification.

questions.question: A prompt tells the model to be brief and also to explain every detail in full. What is this anti-pattern?
options: Conflicting instructions that cancel each other out
Few-shot prompting
Chain-of-thought prompting
Reference-once grounding
questions.explanation: Asking for brevity and a full explanation in the same prompt creates conflicting instructions, which cancel each other out and leave the model to pick one arbitrarily.

questions.question: A team needs every generated email to match their house tone and structure. Which technique should the writer use?
options: Add a longer role description with more adjectives
Raise the model temperature for variety
Remove all constraints so the model can adapt
Provide a few worked input and output examples so the model mimics the format and tone
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting gives the model worked examples of the task, which is the technique for making it mimic a particular tone, structure, or style, whereas adjectives and looser constraints do not set the pattern.

questions.question: To be safe, a writer pastes every field on the record and the entire case history into the prompt. What is the problem?
options: The prompt is now too short to ground the answer
Grounding is not allowed on standard objects
The context becomes over-broad and repeated, which dilutes the signal, so only the facts the answer needs should be injected once
The output shape is now JSON instead of text
questions.explanation: Over-stuffing the prompt with a whole record and its history dilutes the signal and buries the relevant fact, so the better move is to inject the specific facts the answer needs and reference each once.

questions.question: External Community users cannot retrieve from a library that works for internal users. What is the fix?
options: Add the external users to the Manage Data Libraries permission.
Recreate the search index.
Grant Allow View Knowledge to the external users.
Tag the library's data model objects ExternalData.Visibility.Portal or ExternalData.Visibility.Public.
questions.explanation: Internal users are covered by the All Data Access ruleset policy, but external users need the library's data model objects tagged for external visibility.

questions.question: For a file or knowledge based library, when is the retriever created?
options: After chunking completes and the search index is ready.
Before the data stream is created.
When the first user asks a question.
As soon as the library is named and saved.
questions.explanation: The retriever is created only after chunking finishes and the search index is ready, so a stalled index means no retriever exists yet.

questions.question: The chunk records in the index still describe an older version of an article that was edited last week. Which stage is at fault?
options: Chunking, because the chunks are too small
Indexing, because the stored content is stale and the index needs reprocessing
Retriever, because its filter is too tight
Prompt, because the instructions are outdated
questions.explanation: Stored chunks that reflect superseded source text are an indexing fault, and the fix is to reprocess the index so the vectors match the current content.

questions.question: An agent returns a confident but unsupported answer even though the index holds the correct passage. Which hop should you suspect first?
options: The model, because it always ignores provided context
The embedding model, which must be rebuilt every query
The retriever, because a filter, missing field, or inactive retriever can keep the passage from reaching the prompt
The user's query, which cannot be embedded
questions.explanation: When the index is healthy but the answer is unsupported, the retriever is the most likely fault because a tight filter, omitted fields, or an inactive retriever stops the passage from reaching the prompt.

questions.question: An agent returns a fragment of a policy without its exception clause, and the source article plainly states both. Which stage is at fault?
options: The retriever, because it filters the clause out
Chunking, because the split cut the exception away from the rule
The LLM, because it ignored provided context
The embedding model, because it cannot represent exceptions
questions.explanation: When the source contains the full idea but the returned passage is only half of it, the split landed mid-idea, which is a chunking fault proven by inspecting the chunk records.

questions.question: Which data library source creates a retriever but no search index?
options: Uploaded PDF files.
Knowledge articles.
A custom retriever source.
Web search.
questions.explanation: A web search library is read-only and fetches content live, so it creates only a retriever and skips the chunk-and-index chain.

questions.question: A consultant builds a new retriever and wants the agent to ground on the passage text and still cite its source. Which setting supplies that?
options: Setting the data source to Data Cloud
Choosing All Documents as the filter
Returning the Chunks field and enabling Citation Settings
Selecting Vector search as the Search Type
questions.explanation: Returning Chunks gives the model the passage to ground on and Citation Settings lets the agent show its source, while the data source, filter, and search type control scope and matching rather than the returned content and citations.

questions.question: Where does Data 360 store the vector embeddings it produces from chunked content?
options: In a Vector Data Model Object (VDMO)
In the source knowledge article's rich text field
In the prompt template's resource section
In the agent's topic instructions
questions.explanation: Data 360 converts each chunk into a vector embedding and stores it in a Vector Data Model Object, whereas the other locations hold source text, prompt configuration, or agent instructions rather than vectors.

questions.question: Which statement about retrievers and search indexes is correct?
options: A search index can be shared only if the libraries first share a retriever.
A retriever stores the embeddings and the index points to it.
Web search libraries create a search index and a retriever.
Each data library has its own retriever, and retrievers can point to the same search index while each pointer stays unique.
questions.explanation: Each library gets its own retriever, and multiple retrievers may point at one search index, so sharing an index is fine while sharing a retriever is not.

questions.question: Two data libraries need to retrieve different subsets of information from the same indexed content. What does Data 360 do?
options: It builds a separate search index for each library automatically
Each library has its own retriever that can point to the same search index but operates independently
It disables retrieval for the second library
It stores a copy of the vectors inside each prompt template
questions.explanation: Each Agentforce Data Library has its own unique retriever that can point to the same search index but operates independently, so separate indexes, disabled retrieval, or embedded vector copies are all wrong.

questions.question: The index holds current, correctly chunked passages, but the agent grounds on only Titles and URLs and never the passage text. Which stage is at fault?
options: Chunking, because the passages should be larger
Indexing, because the vectors are missing
Retriever configuration, because Fields to Return omit the Chunks the model needs
The LLM, because it cannot read Titles
questions.explanation: A healthy index paired with a retriever that returns Titles and URLs but not Chunks is a retriever configuration fault, fixed in the Fields to Return setting rather than in chunking or indexing.

questions.question: An agent must answer from a specific retriever you configured in Data 360 rather than the auto-built one. What do you use?
options: A custom retriever referenced by your own prompt template.
The Answer Questions with Knowledge action with no retriever input.
A web search data library, which is read-only.
A Knowledge data category on the source article.
questions.explanation: A custom retriever wired into your own prompt template gives control over which datasets are reached, whereas the packaged action uses the retriever Salesforce builds for the library.

questions.question: A requirement says the transfer action must be impossible to call until every validation passes. Which mechanism delivers that guarantee?
options: A prompt line telling the model to wait
A variable holding a note about the state
A template expression showing the balance
An available when filter on the action that stays false until the gating variable is set
questions.explanation: Only an available when clause removes the action from the model's tool list until the gating variable is true, whereas prompt wording and an ungated variable note can both be bypassed.

questions.question: A customer-service agent that works well in live chat is connected to email and starts failing. What is the most likely reason?
options: Email requires a different agent type
Email is turn-based with no live session, so conversation variables the agent expects are not carried across messages
Email cannot reach the agent at all
The agent needs more standard actions
questions.explanation: Email runs through Email-to-Case as a turn-based interaction without a persistent session, so an agent that assumes a live chat session loses the state it depends on.

questions.question: On a messaging surface, what determines whose data access the service agent uses by default?
options: The customer's browser permissions
The signed-in site user automatically
The dedicated agent user, unless credential-based verification is enabled
The Slack workspace owner
questions.explanation: A service agent typically runs as a dedicated agent user, and only credential-based verification switches it to run as the signed-in site user.

questions.question: In a subagent instruction block, which symbol begins a prompt instruction that the model reads as natural language?
options: A single-line comment marker
A right arrow
An at sign
A vertical bar
questions.explanation: A line beginning with a vertical bar opens a prompt instruction, while a line beginning with a right arrow opens a logic instruction that executes as code.

questions.question: An integration team asks for the base URL to call against when starting an Agentforce agent session. What is the correct answer?
options: The org's instance URL from My Domain
The Experience Cloud site URL
The login URL of the org
A fixed api.salesforce.com host, with the agent endpoints under the /einstein/ai-agent/v1 path, and the instance endpoint passed inside the session payload
questions.explanation: Agent API is served from the fixed api.salesforce.com base, and the org's instance endpoint is supplied in the start session payload rather than used as the API base.

questions.question: What must be true of any variable that controls an available when gate?
options: The model sets it fresh on every turn
It must be a string type
It must be declared linked to an external source
It must have a deterministic code path that sets it, rather than relying on the model
questions.explanation: A gate variable must be set by code, in before_reasoning or through a run and set sequence, because a variable the model may or may not set makes the gate as random as the model.

questions.question: A retailer wants an agent on its public website where anonymous shoppers ask about returns, and signed-in shoppers must see only their own orders. What does the consultant build?
options: A Service agent on an enhanced messaging channel, with credential-based user verification so signed-in shoppers run as their own site user
An Employee agent assigned to each shopper
A Lead Nurturing agent
An Employee agent deployed in Slack
questions.explanation: External website shoppers belong to a Service agent, and credential-based verification is the mechanism that makes a signed-in shopper run as their own site user so they see only their own orders.

questions.question: A request lands in no topic at all. Which part of the configuration is the first suspect?
options: The action's Apex class
The topic's action list
The set of classification descriptions, for a job nobody clearly owns
The feedback survey
questions.explanation: Routing into a topic runs on the classification description, so a request that reaches no topic usually means no description clearly covers that job.

questions.question: You must ensure a risky action cannot be called until a validation passes. Which mechanism do you use?
options: A longer, more forceful prompt instruction
A knowledge retriever on the action
An available when condition on the action that is false until the controlling variable is set
A second model call to check the state
questions.explanation: An available when condition is a platform gate that removes the action from the tool list until the variable is true, whereas a prompt instruction is only a suggestion the model may ignore.

questions.question: Your Agent Script is compiled and run. Which statement describes the artifact the runtime actually executes?
options: The Canvas blocks directly
The raw prompt text
The Agentforce Builder editing session
The Agent Graph, a serialized execution plan the Atlas Reasoning Engine traverses as a state machine
questions.explanation: The compiler turns Agent Script into the Agent Graph, and the Atlas Reasoning Engine executes that graph as a state machine, not the Canvas blocks or the prompt text.

questions.question: An external service wants to call the agent and immediately use a structured value the agent's action produced, without dealing with a chat UI. Which shape fits?
options: An Employee agent in Slack
Agent API in a single-turn synchronous call, reading the structured output variables from the response
A prompt template in Prompt Builder
A public Service agent with no integration
questions.explanation: The caller wants a programmatic request-response with structured output, which is exactly the synchronous Agent API pattern, not a chat surface.

questions.question: A developer plans to pass an account id into the conversation after the session has already started, as context for the agent's reasoning. What should the consultant advise?
options: Set the context variables the reasoning needs in the start session call, because context variables are read-only after the session begins
Add them to the first message, since context sets at any time
Store them in a Flow variable
Change the instance endpoint mid session
questions.explanation: Most context variables are read-only once the session starts, so the starting context belongs in the start session payload rather than the first message.

questions.question: Where should a business rule that must always behave the same way live?
options: In the topic instructions
In the action's own Flow or Apex logic
In the classification description
In the agent's welcome message
questions.explanation: Topic and action instructions are non-deterministic, so deterministic or sensitive rules belong inside the action's Flow or Apex, where they always execute the same way.

questions.question: A service team wants an agent that handles customer chats on the company website and hands hard cases to a human agent. Which type and running identity fit?
options: An Employee agent running as the logged-in rep
A Lead Nurturing agent sending email
A Service agent on an enhanced messaging channel, running as the Agent User and escalating to a human when the case is complex
A retired Agentforce (Default) agent
questions.explanation: External customer chats arrive with no Salesforce login, so a Service agent runs as the Agent User and hands complicated cases to a human. An Employee agent would require the caller to be an authenticated internal user.

questions.question: A prompt instruction tells the model to always run a validation action first, but in production the model sometimes skips it. What is the correct fix?
options: Rewrite the prompt in stronger language
Add a second model call to double-check
Move the run into before_reasoning so it executes unconditionally
Turn off hybrid reasoning for that subagent
questions.explanation: A prompt line is only a suggestion the model may skip, whereas moving the run into before_reasoning makes it code that executes on every parse.

questions.question: An anonymous shopper chats on a website and then logs in mid conversation, after which they must see only their own orders. What makes that possible?
options: Setting a context variable with the shopper's email
A context variable identifies the user but does not control access, so credential-based verification switches the session to the verified site user whose sharing rules limit the data
Assigning the shopper to a profile by hand
Nothing, because a Service agent always sees all orders
questions.explanation: Context tells the agent who the person claims to be, but access is governed by the running identity, which only switches to the verified site user once credential-based verification succeeds.

questions.question: An external service authenticates with the client credentials flow and has no interactive user. Which session setting makes the agent run correctly?
options: Set bypassUser to true so the session uses the agent's own user
Set bypassUser to false and rely on the shared token user
Leave bypassUser out and let it default
Disable the session entirely
questions.explanation: The client credentials flow has no interactive user, so the session should run as the agent user, which is what bypassUser set to true selects.

questions.question: An agent keeps firing Get Task Details when the user wants project information. Both actions exist in the same topic. What is the best fix?
options: Remove the project action from the topic
Rename the actions so their verbs and descriptions clearly separate what each does
Move both actions into topic instructions
Add a validation rule on the Task object
questions.explanation: The model separates actions largely by name and description, so distinct, verb-led names and clear descriptions resolve the confusion better than removing the action.

questions.question: A support manager asks for an agent that lets signed-in customers on a portal view their own past cases and open a new one. Which type and mechanism fit?
options: A Service agent on an enhanced messaging channel with credential-based verification, so the signed-in customer runs as their own site user and sees only their cases
An Employee agent assigned to each customer
A Lead Nurturing agent
A retired Agentforce (Default) agent
questions.explanation: The audience is external customers, so it is a Service agent, and credential-based verification is what limits each customer to their own records rather than the agent user's broader access.

questions.question: Which is a stated benefit of pushing work onto the deterministic path?
options: The model becomes more accurate at reasoning
The agent gains new actions automatically
Fewer model calls, which removes latency and variability and lowers cost
Audit logging is disabled for deterministic actions
questions.explanation: Nodes without prompt instructions execute as code, so removing model calls removes latency and variability and lowers cost, and it never disables audit logging.

questions.question: How is Agent Script presented in Canvas view?
options: Summarized into understandable blocks you can expand to view the underlying script
As the compiled Agent Graph only
As raw JSON with no editing
As a Flow diagram of each action
questions.explanation: Canvas view summarizes Agent Script into blocks you can expand to see the script underneath, while the Agent Graph is a separate compiled artifact the runtime executes.

questions.question: Which statement matches how Testing Center sits alongside the testing you do in Agentforce Builder?
options: Builder preview and Live Test debug a single conversation, while Testing Center runs a suite of cases to score breadth before a release
Testing Center replaces Live Test, which is retired
Builder Live Test requires a CSV upload before it will run
Testing Center runs only from the legacy Setup page
questions.explanation: Builder tests one conversation in real time, including actions against real records, while Testing Center runs many cases to measure routing, actions, and response quality at scale.

questions.question: Which set of cases gives the most useful test of an agent that is already live?
options: Cases generated only from subagent metadata, because they match the configuration
One long conversation that walks through every subagent in order
Utterances pulled from real sessions in Agent Analytics and Session Trace, including typos, topic changes, and half-formed requests
Cases written by the product owner from the requirements document
questions.explanation: Real session utterances carry the phrasing customers actually use, which is where routing and response failures show up, while tidy generated or authored cases test the agent you designed.

questions.question: Which of these pieces of an agent setup is re-established in production rather than migrated, and is the reason an agent can work in the sandbox and fail after go-live?
options: The subagent instructions
The default system messages
The variables and filters defined on the template
Authentication to an external data vendor connection, which is per org
questions.explanation: External connections and their authentication are scoped to the org, so they do not travel with the agent and must be re-established in production, unlike the portable definitions such as instructions, messages, variables, and filters.

questions.question: An action assertion passes for a conversation-level test. What did it actually verify?
options: That every expected action occurred, even though the agent may also have performed extra actions
That the agent performed exactly the expected actions and nothing else
That the underlying records were updated correctly
That the actions ran under the running user's permissions
questions.explanation: The conversation-level action rule is that the test passes when all expected actions occurred, so extra actions do not fail it and record updates are not checked.

questions.question: A service agent is active and answering in the builder, but customers cannot reach it from the company website. Which step was most likely missed?
options: Publish the Embedded Service Deployment for the channel in the target org
Retrieve the agent metadata a second time
Re-create the agent user with a new username
Deploy the agent a second time with the root-type-with-dependencies flag removed
questions.explanation: Channel plumbing such as Embedded Service Deployments is separate from the agent metadata, so an agent that is active but unreachable is usually missing the channel step and the web deployment publish.

questions.question: You generated multi-turn test cases from your subagents and want each case to open with prior turns the agent must carry. What must you do?
options: Regenerate the set with history enabled, because generated cases already include the prior turns
Add the turns as context variables on the case
Switch the suite to Mocked Data so history is applied
Add the preceding utterances to the conversation history column yourself, because conversation history is a column in the downloadable CSV template and is not factored into generated test cases
questions.explanation: Conversation history is a CSV template column that generated cases do not include, so a multi-turn scenario needs those turns written in by hand.

questions.question: A response reads fluently and answers the question, but it cites the wrong knowledge article. Which Quality Score signal points at this?
options: Low Context Relevance, because the agent retrieved the wrong source for the question
Low Adherence Response Rate, because the agent ignored its instructions
High Abandonment Rate, because the user disengaged
Low Success Rate, because an action step errored
questions.explanation: Context Relevance scores whether the correct source was retrieved, so a fluent answer grounded on the wrong document shows there.

questions.question: What does committing an agent version do?
options: It publishes the version to every connected channel immediately
It merges the version into the active version's draft history
It deletes the previous version from Agentforce Builder
It saves a snapshot of the version to metadata and makes it available to activate, after which the version can no longer be edited
questions.explanation: Commit writes a frozen snapshot to metadata so the version can be activated, and the freeze is what stops you editing it afterward.

questions.question: Three days after a launch, an operator filters the Sessions and Intents page and finds no intents at all. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The sessions were deleted by the retention policy
The agent is not connected to any channel
The operator lacks the permission to see intents
No intent group has yet reached the cluster threshold, because intents are generated daily and clustered weekly
questions.explanation: Intents are generated daily and clustered weekly, and a group with too few matching intents does not form a cluster, so an empty list early in a launch is expected.

questions.question: Success Rate drops and the Trace shows an error step where an action fails for some users. Which statement best explains it?
options: The agent's instructions are too vague and need rewriting
The action fails at run time because it runs under each user's security context, so check the action's inputs and permissions
The knowledge article behind the action is out of date
The metric is lagging and the drop is not real
questions.explanation: An error step in an action points at the action and its inputs, and because actions run under the running user's security context a missing permission fails them at run time.

questions.question: Which metric is defined as the share of sessions that ended without escalation to a support representative or another agent?
options: Success Rate
Engagement Rate
Deflection Rate
Abandonment Rate
questions.explanation: Deflection Rate is the share of sessions that ended without escalation, which is distinct from abandonment and engagement.

questions.question: An agent routes every returns request correctly to the Returns subagent, but the replies are too terse and miss detail the customer asked for. The Trace shows no errors. Which lever do you change?
options: The subagent's instructions, because the routing is correct and the answer quality is the problem
The topic scope, because the request should route elsewhere
The action inputs, because a step failed
The knowledge source, because retrieval returned nothing
questions.explanation: Correct routing with weak answers points at the instructions, while a failing step or wrong retrieval would point at actions or knowledge instead.

questions.question: In a single-org multi-agent design, which agent can escalate a conversation to a human?
options: Only the orchestrator agent
Only the connected subagent that owns the record
Any agent in the design
An escalation agent added as an extra subagent
questions.explanation: Only the orchestrator agent can escalate to a human, so human handoff is centralised at the front door rather than handled by connected subagents.

questions.question: Which statement about the Agent-to-Agent Protocol is correct?
options: It is an open protocol for agent-to-agent communication, and Salesforce was a founding member alongside Google, Microsoft, SAP, and AWS
It is a Salesforce proprietary protocol for in-org subagents
It is a tool interface that exposes external APIs as callable actions
It is a data store for Agentforce reasoning traces
questions.explanation: A2A is an open, cross-vendor protocol for peer agent communication, and Salesforce was a founding member of the effort, so it is not a proprietary or tool-level construct.

questions.question: An Agentforce agent must reach an external system that is not MCP-enabled. What does the documented architecture use to expose it?
options: MuleSoft acts as an MCP wrapper that exposes the API as MCP tools
A2A Agent Cards are generated automatically for the API
The agent calls the native API directly with no wrapper
A connected subagent replaces the external system
questions.explanation: Where a remote system is not MCP-enabled, MuleSoft acts as an MCP wrapper that exposes those APIs as MCP tools, which is why the missing wrapper blocks the call.
